A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RIFLEx research. All 19 pages, including Appendices A–F, equations, tables, and figures, are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original video-generation experiments, quantitative comparisons and a 10-participant user study in Section 4, alongside frequency analyses and appendix demonstrations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments, user-study outcomes, frequency analyses, and appendix results.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same intrinsic-frequency identification and reduction procedure. Fine-tuning and spatial adaptation are also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same private fine-tuning dataset, VBench prompts, and 100 HunyuanVideo prompts. Temporal, spatial, and joint extrapolation coverage remains unchanged, including appendix scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains PE, NTK, PI, TASR, and YaRN in the corresponding training-free comparisons, PE in fine-tuned comparisons, and NTK in the HunyuanVideo 2.3× comparison. Appendix comparator membership is also unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.1, Appendix D, and Table 3 retain identical model configurations, training budgets, resolutions, batch sizes, metrics, NoRepeat threshold of 100, and user-ranking procedures.

E4.justification: Both retain the frequency-isolation and fine-tuning analyses, 4× extrapolation failure examples, and Appendix E's 20-video consistency analysis and frequency ablations. No analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Point-score and user-ranking reporting is unchanged. Neither version provides repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 1's values and rankings and all plotted and qualitative results are unchanged, including the appendices. For example, HunyuanVideo 2.3× NoRepeat scores remain 54.0 for RIFLEx and 20.0 for NTK.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(8), the intrinsic-frequency definition, and the non-repetition derivation are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, propositions, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about intrinsic frequency, training-free 2× extrapolation, minimally fine-tuned 3× extrapolation, and spatial applicability.

C2.justification: The explanations of repetition, slow motion, and extrapolation degradation remain identical. Section 5 retains the limitations concerning visual frequency identification, missing theoretical foundations, and degradation beyond 3× extrapolation.

D1.justification: Appendix D and Tables 2–3 retain the same implementation instructions, hyperparameters, hardware, code links, and code licenses. The project/code access statement is also unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to Zhao et al. (2022), EGSDE; Zhao et al. (2023), ControlVideo; and Zhao et al. (2024), conditional image leakage. These enter citation lists in the introduction and Appendix A without substantive new discussion or changed novelty positioning.

P1.justification: Edits are limited to citation lists, bibliography additions, and the arXiv version/date notice. Explanatory prose, terminology, section order, and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Additional citations and references cause local line, column, and page-break reflow on pages 1–3 and 12–13. All 13 figures and three tables retain their content, design, and placement.

improvement.justification: v3 slightly expands the bibliography but adds no substantive discussion, evidence, or reproducibility information. The scientific arguments, experimental support, and acknowledged limitations remain unchanged, while the layout adjustments have no meaningful effect on readability.
